extraction.name: tiny images dataset
extraction.description: A dataset of 80 million colour images downscaled to 32×32, collected from the web by searching for every non-abstract English noun in WordNet. The search term provides a rough but unreliable label, and the dataset was used for experiments in unsupervised learning.
extraction.creator: colleagues at MIT and NYU
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was assembled by searching the web for images corresponding to every non-abstract English noun in WordNet, using several search engines, keeping roughly the first 3000 results per term, then removing perfect duplicates and overly white/synthetic images. The paper also created reliable labels for subsets (CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100).
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Millions of tiny color images from the web; in total 80 million color images downscaled to 32x32 across 79,000 search terms, with rough labels derived from the search terms.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Over the span of six months
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The paper states that the authors created two sets of reliable labels for CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, and indicates there is a 'Labeler instruction sheet,' but the provided excerpt does not describe the labeling task, instructions, workforce, or quality control in detail.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset has unreliable rough labels derived from web search terms, and image collection reflects biases of online image search and human photography composition.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The tiny images dataset is difficult for learning good filters, and its labels are not reliable enough for object recognition experiments without creating new reliable labeled subsets.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Language-related metadata is implicitly used through English noun search terms from WordNet.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is used for unsupervised training of deep generative models and for object recognition/classification experiments using the CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 labeled subsets; pretrained features are used to improve classifiers.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Used a subset of about 2 million images from the 80 million Tiny Images dataset; split each 32x32 image into 25 overlapping 8x8 patches plus a 26th 8x8 subsampled global patch; later merged 26 independently trained patch-based RBMs into one larger RBM.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Removed perfect duplicates and images with excessively large white regions; downscaled images to 32x32; applied ZCA whitening to decorrelate pixels; additionally removed the 1000 least-significant principal components by setting those variance directions to zero.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: previous researchers who have tried this have found it difficult to learn a good set of filters from the images. A second problematic aspect of the tiny images dataset is that there are no reliable class labels which makes it hard to use for object recognition experiments.

rai:personalSensitiveInformation.evidence: They assembled it by searching the web for images of every non-abstract English noun in the lexical database WordNet

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: it is, in principle, an excellent dataset for unsupervised training of deep generative models ... We created two sets of reliable labels. The CIFAR-10 set has 6000 examples of each of 10 classes and the CIFAR-100 set has 600 examples of each of 100 non-overlapping classes. Using these labels, we show that object recognition is significantly improved by pre-training a layer of features on a large set of unlabeled tiny images.

rai:dataManipulationProtocol.evidence: “Most of our experiments with unsupervised learning were performed on a subset of about 2 million images.”; “We divided the 32×32 images into 25 8×8 patches... In addition to the patches shown in Figure 2.4, we created a 26th patch: an 8×8 subsampled version of the entire 32×32 image.”; “Once we have trained 26 of these RBMs on the tiny image patches, we can combine them... by training a new RBM with 7800 (26×300) hidden units.”

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: “they removed perfect duplicates and images in which an excessively large portion of the pixels were white”; “the dataset contains 80 million colour images downscaled to 32×32”; “this can be done with a data preprocessing step that just consists of multiplying the data matrix by a whitening matrix”; “We accomplished this by setting to zero those entries of the diagonal matrix D... that correspond to the 1000 least significant principal components.”
